body:
What engineering industries manufacture

Engineering industries make machines, equipment and components used by other industries and by consumers. They include the manufacture of pumps, motors, castings, valves, fasteners, machine parts and industrial equipment.

Many engineering products are not sold directly to households. A pump may be installed in a factory, a machined component may become part of a vehicle, and an electrical terminal may be fitted inside another manufactured product. Components incorporated into other products are intermediate goods, while a pump used repeatedly in a factory is a capital good.

Gujarat has significant engineering activity around Rajkot, while Jamnagar is widely associated with the manufacture of brass components. These industries include many small and medium enterprises serving larger manufacturers and other markets.

Why the properties of metals matter

Metals are useful for engineering because many of them conduct heat and electricity, can withstand mechanical loads and can be shaped into required forms.

  • Malleability is the ability of a material to be hammered or rolled into sheets without breaking.
  • Ductility is the ability to be drawn into wires.
  • Electrical conductivity is important for products such as wires, terminals and electrical connectors.
  • Strength and corrosion resistance influence the suitability of materials for machinery, fittings and other applications.

These properties are not identical in every metal. The material selected depends on what the finished component must do.

Three basic ways of making metal components

Engineering firms may produce metal parts by casting, forging or machining. These processes work differently.

ProcessBasic principleExample of use
CastingMolten material is poured into a mould and allowed to solidify.Producing components with a required cast shape
ForgingMetal is shaped by compressive force, usually while solid.Producing strong, shaped metal components
MachiningMaterial is removed from a workpiece to obtain the required shape or finish.Producing precisely shaped or fitted parts

A cast component may still require machining before use. Therefore, the processes can be successive stages of one supply chain rather than mutually exclusive alternatives.

Rajkot's engineering industries

Rajkot has a long-established engineering and machine-component manufacturing base. Associated activities include foundries, castings, machine tools, pumps, diesel-engine-related products and automobile components.

A foundry is an industrial establishment that produces metal castings. Once casting units become established, nearby enterprises may develop to provide moulding materials, machine tools, repair services and finishing operations.

Rajkot's industrial system also demonstrates the relationship between large factories and smaller suppliers. A small enterprise may specialise in one casting, bearing or machined part rather than manufacture the complete machine or vehicle.

Jamnagar's brass industry

Brass is an alloy made mainly from copper and zinc. It is used in products such as plumbing fittings, electrical accessories, valves and decorative hardware. An alloy is a material formed by combining a metal with one or more other elements to obtain useful properties.

Jamnagar has a major cluster of enterprises producing brass parts through activities that include casting, extrusion, machining and finishing. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency identifies Jamnagar as an important brass-manufacturing cluster.

Jamnagar is also known for petroleum refining, but its brass engineering industry and petroleum-refining industry are separate industrial activities. Their presence in the same city or district must not be confused with similarity in their raw materials or production processes.

Basic manufacturing technology and sustainability

Computer Numerical Control (CNC) uses computer-based instructions to control the movements of suitable machine tools. It can help produce components consistently and accurately. CNC machining is different from additive manufacturing, commonly called 3D printing, which builds an object by adding material rather than primarily removing it.

Foundries and metal-processing units use energy for heating, melting and machining. Important environmental concerns include furnace emissions, dust, industrial waste and energy consumption. Energy efficiency and suitable waste recovery can reduce material loss and operating costs.

Prelims focus

  • Rajkot is associated with engineering, foundries, machinery and automobile components.
  • Jamnagar is a major brass-parts manufacturing cluster.
  • Brass is principally an alloy of copper and zinc.
  • Casting uses molten material; forging shapes metal under compressive force; machining removes material.
  • CNC refers to computer-controlled machine-tool operation.
  • Trap: Jamnagar's brass industry should not be confused with its petroleum-refining industry.

[NCERT, Class 8 Science, Chapter 4, Materials: Metals and Non-Metals, printed pp. 44–46; Bureau of Energy Efficiency and UNIDO, Promoting Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy in Selected MSME Clusters in India, Brass Sector, Jamnagar Cluster Profile, consulted 14 November 2026; Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Selected MSME Cluster Details, Rajkot engineering-related cluster information, consulted 14 November 2026.]

body:
An automobile factory depends on many industries

An automobile is assembled from a large number of components. It requires metal parts, tyres, glass, plastics, electrical wiring, electronic controls and many other products. Automobile manufacturing therefore creates demand for engineering, chemical, electronics and materials industries.

The company that assembles and sells the finished vehicle is commonly called an original equipment manufacturer (OEM). It generally obtains many parts from specialised suppliers. Some suppliers manufacture parts directly for the vehicle manufacturer; others supply smaller components or materials to those firms.

A strong automobile cluster is not merely a collection of vehicle assembly plants. It also includes component makers, testing facilities, transport services, skilled technicians and supporting industries.

Major automobile locations in Gujarat

Gujarat's automobile manufacturing activity is notably associated with the Sanand–Khoraj area near Ahmedabad, the Mandal–Becharaji region including the Hansalpur area, and the Halol region. Rajkot's engineering enterprises also contribute to automobile-component supply chains.

These industrial concentrations benefit from transport connections, industrial land, engineering suppliers and proximity to other manufacturing centres. Large vehicle manufacturers can stimulate the growth of smaller component units in nearby areas.

The Mandal–Becharaji Special Investment Region is an industrial-development area associated with automobile manufacturing. The term Special Investment Region describes a planned regional development framework. It should not be confused with a particular vehicle manufacturer or with the whole of Gujarat's automobile industry.

The automobile supply chain

Different enterprises contribute at successive stages:

  • Materials producers supply steel, aluminium, plastics, rubber and other materials.
  • Component manufacturers make engines or motors, bearings, castings, wiring, lamps and many other parts.
  • Vehicle assemblers combine the components into finished automobiles.
  • Logistics and distribution firms transport components and finished vehicles.
  • Repair, reuse and recycling enterprises provide services during and after a vehicle's useful life.

A factory producing automobile components is part of the automotive supply chain even when it does not manufacture a complete vehicle.

Internal-combustion and electric vehicles

An internal-combustion-engine vehicle obtains mechanical energy by burning fuel inside an engine. It typically requires a fuel system, engine and exhaust-related components.

A battery electric vehicle (BEV) stores electrical energy in a rechargeable battery and uses one or more electric motors for propulsion. Important components include the battery pack, electric motor, power electronics and a battery-management system.

FeatureInternal-combustion vehicleBattery electric vehicle
Main onboard energy sourcePetrol, diesel or another suitable fuelElectricity stored in a rechargeable battery
PropulsionInternal-combustion engineElectric motor
Important associated componentsFuel system and exhaust-related equipmentBattery pack, motor controller and power electronics
Tailpipe emissions during useProduced by combustionNo combustion-related tailpipe emissions

A battery electric vehicle has no combustion-related tailpipe emissions, but producing its battery and generating electricity can still create environmental impacts. The total environmental effect depends on manufacturing, electricity sources, vehicle use and recycling.

Why electric mobility changes manufacturing demand

The shift towards electric vehicles increases demand for battery cells and packs, electric motors, power-electronic devices and specialised electrical components. It can reduce the need for some conventional engine and exhaust components in fully electric vehicles.

This change creates opportunities for existing engineering enterprises to diversify. However, a factory skilled in making conventional metal parts does not automatically possess the technology required to manufacture battery cells or semiconductor devices.

A relevant national programme

The Government of India's PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) scheme was notified in September 2024 to support electric mobility and related infrastructure. The Ministry of Heavy Industries' official portal records an enhancement of its outlay and an extension of the overall scheme period to 31 March 2028, except for the e-3W (L5) segment, which closed on 26 December 2025; the deadline for submitting claims is 31 December 2027.

PM E-DRIVE is primarily associated with promoting electric mobility and supporting infrastructure. It should not be interpreted as a scheme that automatically establishes an automobile factory in a particular city.

Prelims focus

  • Sanand–Khoraj and Mandal–Becharaji are important Gujarat automobile-manufacturing areas.
  • Halol is another established automobile-manufacturing location.
  • Rajkot contributes engineering and automobile components.
  • An OEM assembles or supplies the finished branded vehicle; specialised firms may supply its components.
  • A battery electric vehicle uses a rechargeable battery and electric motor rather than a conventional combustion engine for propulsion.
  • Trap: Automobile assembly and automobile-component manufacturing are different stages of the same supply chain.

[Vibrant Gujarat, Auto and Auto Components sector profile, sections Infrastructure and Manufacturing Ecosystem, consulted 14 November 2026; Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation, Industrial Estate Allotment Directory, FY 2026–27, Ahmedabad industrial estates, consulted 14 November 2026; Ministry of Heavy Industries, PM E-DRIVE Scheme, About the Scheme and amendments through 10 August 2026, consulted 14 November 2026.]

body:
Why semiconductors matter to manufacturing

Semiconductors are materials whose electrical behaviour lies between that of good conductors and insulators and can be controlled for electronic applications. Silicon is the most familiar semiconductor material.

Semiconductor devices perform functions such as switching, controlling and processing electrical signals. They are essential in computers, mobile phones, industrial machines, communication equipment and modern vehicles.

Electronics manufacturing includes several activities: producing electronic components, manufacturing semiconductor devices, assembling circuit boards and making finished electronic products. These activities are related but do not all require the same factory processes.

Fabrication is different from assembly and testing

A major distinction in semiconductor manufacturing is between wafer fabrication and assembly, testing and packaging.

A semiconductor fabrication plant, often called a fab, produces electronic devices on semiconductor wafers. A wafer is a thin disc of semiconductor material on which numerous device structures can be manufactured.

Once devices are fabricated, they generally require additional processing. Assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP) operations prepare semiconductor devices for practical use. Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) describes a business model in which specialised enterprises provide assembly, packaging and testing services.

Packaging helps protect the semiconductor device and allows it to connect with other electronic components. Testing checks whether it meets required performance conditions. These operations are technically important, but they are not the same as manufacturing semiconductor devices on a blank wafer.

Fab versus ATMP or OSAT: A fab manufactures semiconductor devices on wafers. ATMP and OSAT operations assemble, package and test devices. Opening a packaging plant does not automatically mean a wafer-fabrication plant has begun producing chips at that location.

Sanand's semiconductor assembly and testing facilities

Sanand, near Ahmedabad, has developed important semiconductor assembly, packaging and testing activity.

The following are dated official milestones relevant to the content cutoff of 14 November 2026:

  • 28 February 2026: The Government of India inaugurated Micron Technology's semiconductor ATMP facility at Sanand. The official announcement reported the commencement of commercial production and shipment of semiconductor memory products.
  • 31 March 2026: Kaynes Semicon's facility at Sanand was inaugurated. The official announcement described the commencement of production at the facility.
  • 4 July 2026: The CG Semi OSAT facility at Sanand was inaugurated. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology reported the commencement of commercial production.

These milestones concern semiconductor assembly, packaging and testing. They should not be treated as evidence that each company operates a silicon-wafer fabrication plant.

Dholera's semiconductor fabrication project

Dholera is associated with the development of a major semiconductor fabrication project by Tata Electronics in technology partnership with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC).

The Government of India approved the project in February 2024. Official project information identifies a planned capacity of approximately 50,000 wafer starts per month. This figure is a project capacity, not a count of semiconductor chips already produced.

On 16 April 2026, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry announced that a Special Economic Zone for the Tata semiconductor project at Dholera had been notified. The notification concerned industrial development and the legal status of the zone; it was not an announcement of commercial semiconductor production.

A Press Information Bureau backgrounder dated 28 September 2026 described the development of supporting infrastructure around the Dholera semiconductor manufacturing cluster. On the evidence of these official announcements, the fab is appropriately described as an approved project under development, rather than a commercially operating wafer fab, at the selected cutoff.

Policies supporting the electronics ecosystem

The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) supports the development of a domestic semiconductor and display-manufacturing ecosystem through national schemes.

The Government of Gujarat has also adopted the Gujarat Semiconductor Policy (2022–27) and the Gujarat Electronics Policy (2022–28). A further Gujarat Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy was issued on 22 June 2025. These policies seek to encourage investment, industrial infrastructure and electronics-related manufacturing.

Semiconductor manufacturing requires reliable electricity, suitable water supply, highly specialised equipment, skilled workers and carefully controlled production conditions. This explains why an emerging semiconductor cluster needs more than a single factory building.

How electronics connects with older Gujarat industries

The growing semiconductor industry creates possible demand for industrial gases, chemicals, precision components, electrical equipment, logistics and infrastructure services. However, ordinary industrial chemicals or engineering products do not automatically satisfy the stringent requirements of semiconductor manufacturing. Suppliers must meet the relevant quality and performance requirements before joining these specialised supply chains.

Prelims focus

  • Sanand is associated with semiconductor ATMP and OSAT activity.
  • Micron's Sanand ATMP facility commenced commercial production in February 2026.
  • Kaynes Semicon's Sanand facility began production in March 2026.
  • CG Semi's Sanand OSAT facility commenced commercial production in July 2026.
  • Dholera is the location of the Tata Electronics–PSMC semiconductor fabrication project, approved in February 2024.
  • Trap: Semiconductor fabrication, semiconductor packaging and SEZ notification are 3 different concepts and milestones.

[Press Information Bureau, Micron ATMP Facility Inauguration, 28 February 2026; Press Information Bureau, Kaynes Semicon Plant Inauguration, 31 March 2026; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, CG Semi OSAT Commercial Production Announcement, 4 July 2026; Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government Notifies India's First Chip Fabrication Plant at SEZ Dholera, 16 April 2026; Press Information Bureau, Beyond the Fab: How Dholera Is Building the Ecosystem Around India's Semiconductor Ambition, 28 September 2026; Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, Gujarat Semiconductor Policy dated 27 July 2022, Gujarat Electronics Policy 2022–28, and Gujarat Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy dated 22 June 2025; official materials consulted 14 November 2026.]
